B.depoimento: I order the construction of two spearmen in Barcelona to strengthen my home guard. I dispatch armies to the nearby neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona to claim them for my kingdom, initiating my expansion into the peninsula.
B.plano: My immediate goal is to secure the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona to establish a foothold and increase my economic base. I will send mixed forces to capture them while reinforcing my capital with newly built spearmen. In the coming turns, I will explore the roads leading east to Zaragoza and Huesca to locate more villages and the enemy, while maintaining a strong garrison in Barcelona.

A.depoimento: I have ordered my armies to take the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora to expand my kingdom's borders. Meanwhile, the forges of Lisboa work overtime to produce more spearman for the coming campaigns.
A.plano: Expand to Santarem and Evora to secure resources and increase my village count. Build spearmen in Lisboa to reinforce the army. Next turn, assess the outcomes and push further along the road network to explore and claim more territory.

A.depoimento: This turn, I ordered the construction of a knight in my capital, Lisboa. I sent archers to take Coimbra and knights to take Faro, securing two new villages and opening up new routes. I also reinforced Santarem with spearman and a knight from Lisboa to prepare for further expansion.
A.plano: Conquer Coimbra and Faro to expand territory and secure resources. Reinforce Santarem with troops from Lisboa to prepare for the next wave of expansion towards the north and east. Build a knight in Lisboa to maintain army growth.

A.depoimento: The time to expand has come! My knights strike at Badajoz, while my spearman push into Porto. With these conquests, I secure vital resources and begin the march towards the enemy's territory.
A.plano: Conquer Badajoz and Porto this turn to expand my territory and secure resources. Send 2 knights from Faro to Badajoz, and 6 spearman from Santarem to Porto via Coimbra. Build 2 spearman in Santarem and Evora, and 1 knight in Lisboa to replenish losses and prepare for the next expansion towards Salamanca and Sevilha.

B.depoimento: I ordered the construction of knights at all my villages and launched attacks on Castellon and Huesca. I also sent reinforcements from Barcelona to Tarragona to prepare for the next assault on Zaragoza.
B.plano: My campaign is to expand aggressively by capturing nearby neutral villages to grow my economy and army. This turn I take Castellon and Huesca while reinforcing Tarragona from Barcelona. Next turn I will attack Zaragoza and push toward Madrid, then continue west to challenge the enemy.

A.depoimento: Turn 5: I strengthened my defenses against enemy attacks and sent reinforcements to aid my troops at Porto. I am building archers across my lands to prepare for the next wave of conquest.
A.plano: Reinforced Coimbra with 2 spearmen from Santarem, and Santarem with 2 knights from Lisboa. Sent 1 knight from Santarem to Porto to assist the 6 spearmen already marching there. Sent 2 spearmen from Evora to Faro to give it a garrison. Built archers in all resource-producing villages to prepare for the next expansion. Next turn: check if Porto fell; if so, explore from Porto. If not, regroup and attack again. Also watch for enemy movements.

A.depoimento: We are finally taking the fight to Porto! Coimbra's finest march to conquer the first neutral village. Meanwhile, we reinforce our borders and build up our forces across the realm to prepare for the next wave of conquest.
A.plano: Attack Porto with Coimbra's troops to secure our first neutral village. Reinforce Coimbra with Santarem's archer, Santarem with Lisboa's archer, and Faro with Evora's spearmen and Badajoz's knights. Build archers in Lisboa and Evora, knights in Santarem, and spearmen in Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro to grow our army for the next expansion.

B.depoimento: Our armies have mobilized to attack the neutral villages of Castellon and Zaragoza. Troops from Barcelona and Girona marched to reinforce our main strike forces in Tarragona and Huesca, aiming to secure new territory and grow our strength.
B.plano: We are focusing on expanding into the neutral villages of Castellon and Zaragoza to secure our borders and increase our resource income. We are concentrating our forces from Barcelona and Girona into Tarragona and Huesca to launch these attacks. After capturing these villages, we will push further into the unexplored territory towards Madrid and the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: This turn we built spearmen in Coimbra and Badajoz, knights in Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, and archers in Faro. We moved Coimbra's troops to Porto, Santarem's to Coimbra, Lisboa's archer to Santarem, Badajoz's spearman to Coimbra, Evora's archers to Faro, and sent Faro's army to attack Seuilha. We are preparing a strong assault on Salamanca next turn.
A.plano: Next turn: send Porto's combined force (2 spear, 2 arch + arriving Coimbra troops) to Salamanca. Send Coimbra's new spearman to Porto. Send Santarem's new knight to Coimbra. Monitor Badajoz's spearman marching to Coimbra and Faro's army marching to Seuilha. Build more spearman and archers as needed.

B.depoimento: We launched a strong assault on Zaragoza with knights and archers from Tarragona, aiming to break the neutral garrison and secure a gateway to the north. Our forces are rebuilding across the realm, preparing for the next push into unexplored lands.
B.plano: Focus on capturing Zaragoza (17) to secure the northern front and open the road to Madrid (12) and Pamplona (19). Concentrate forces from Tarragona and Huesca, rebuild troops in Tarragona, Girona, Barcelona, and Huesca. After Zaragoza, push towards Madrid and Teruel to expand into the unexplored territory.

B.depoimento: I have launched a two-pronged attack from Zaragoza to Madrid and from Castellon to Teruel, leveraging the counter triangle to overcome the defenders. Reinforcements are marching to secure the newly opened fronts and prepare for the next pushes into Pamplona and Valencia.
B.plano: Capture Madrid (12) and Teruel (13) to expand my territory. Reinforce Castellon from Tarragona, Tarragona from Barcelona, Huesca from Girona, and Zaragoza from Huesca to prepare for further expansion into Pamplona (19) and Valencia (16). Build troops in all productive villages to replenish losses and grow the army.

A.depoimento: I have launched a coordinated assault on the neutral villages of Vigo and Salamanca, sending archers and spearmen respectively. I have also sent knights to Badajoz and archers to Sevilha to prepare for the next phase of my expansion into Toledo and Cordoba.
A.plano: Conquer Vigo and Salamanca this turn. Reinforce Badajoz with knights from Santarem and Sevilha with archers from Faro to prepare attacks on Toledo and Cordoba next turn. Build archers in Porto and spearman in Coimbra to enable the attacks.

B.depoimento: I am launching a multi-pronged attack. Valencia and Pamplona are being assaulted, while Teruel's garrison will be wiped out by my first wave, allowing a second wave to capture it. Madrid is being reinforced for the next push west.
B.plano: Capture Valencia and Pamplona this turn. Sacrifice the first wave at Teruel to wipe out the garrison, then send a second wave to capture it. Reinforce Madrid from Zaragoza to prepare for attacks on Burgos and Salamanca next turn. Build troops in all productive villages to replenish losses and grow the army.

A.depoimento: My armies are on the move. I am striking at Cordoba with archers to expand my territory. Salamanca will be secured with reinforcements. I am building up my forces for the next targets, Vigo and Toledo, while replenishing my ranks.
A.plano: Focus on Cordoba and Salamanca. Send 5 archers from Sevilha to Cordoba. Send all Coimbra troops to Salamanca to follow up the 4 spearmen. Build archers in Porto for Vigo, Badajoz for Toledo, and Sevilha/Lisboa/Evora to replenish. Build spearmen in Coimbra and Faro.

A.depoimento: My Coimbra army claims Salamanca. In simultaneous strikes, Porto's archers conquer Vigo and Badajoz's knight-archer force takes Toledo. Sevilha's entire garrison marches to reinforce Cordoba for the push toward Murcia. I build archers and knights across my realm, preparing for the next wave of expansion toward Madrid, Burgos, and Valencia.
A.plano: Turn 11: Salamanca falls to Coimbra's marching army. Porto archers take Vigo. Badajoz knights+archers take Toledo. Sevilha reinforces Cordoba. Build archers everywhere, knights at Evora and Faro. Next turn: attack Madrid (from Salamanca/Toledo), Burgos (from Vigo), Murcia (from Cordoba). Explore unexplored villages. Watch for enemy counterattacks.

B.depoimento: I have launched a bold assault on Burgos, sending every able-bodied soldier from Madrid to capture this key neutral village. In parallel, I am consolidating my eastern forces, gathering a mighty host in Teruel for the imminent attack on Toledo. My factories are working overtime, equipping my armies for the campaigns ahead. The path to the enemy capital is opening, and I will not rest until the map is mine.
B.plano: My campaign focuses on expanding westward and preparing for the push into the enemy heartland. This turn, I conquer Burgos with the full force of Madrid, securing a northern foothold. Simultaneously, I am funneling reinforcements from Zaragoza, Castellon, and Valencia into Teruel to build a massive army. Next turn, I will unleash this army to take Toledo, opening the road to Cordoba and the south. I will continue building troops in all my villages to maintain momentum.

A.depoimento: Our armies strike on all fronts! Salamanca and Toledo converge on Madrid, while Cordoba takes Murcia. Porto reinforces Vigo for the push on Burgos. We build knights in every city to fuel our conquest. The enemy will not stop us!
A.plano: Conquer Madrid and Murcia this turn to reach 14 villages. Send all troops from Salamanca and Toledo to Madrid, and Cordoba to Murcia. Reinforce Vigo with Porto's troops to prepare for Burgos next turn. Reinforce Toledo and Salamanca with Badajoz and Coimbra's archers. Build knights everywhere to maintain momentum. Next turn: attack Burgos from Vigo, explore Zaragoza from Madrid.

B.depoimento: King B's armies move with the speed of a storm! From Teruel, my elite knights and spearmen crash against Toledo; from Burgos, my forces sweep down on Vigo. I am concentrating the might of my entire kingdom on the western front, emptying the rear villages to feed the invasion. The enemy will not hold their ground!
B.plano: This turn, I launch a double-pronged attack: Toledo from Teruel and Vigo from Burgos, aiming to secure two enemy villages and bring my total to 13. I am funneling almost all available troops from the eastern and northern villages (Barcelona, Tarragona, Girona, Huesca, Pamplona, Valencia, Castellon) into the border regions of Zaragoza, Teruel, and Madrid to create an overwhelming force. Next turn, I will attack Salamanca from Madrid with the arriving reinforcements, and then push deeper into the unexplored enemy territory towards Cordoba and the capital Lisboa, working towards the 18-village vi

A.depoimento: We have successfully consolidated our western borders and captured Madrid, Murcia, and Vigo. This turn, we launch our eastern campaign by sending the full garrison of Murcia to crush the weak defense of Valencia. Simultaneously, we are massing our forces at Badajoz, Madrid, Vigo, and Cordoba, reinforcing them from our interior villages to prepare for a decisive push into Toledo and Burgos next turn. The enemy will not be able to stop our combined arms!
A.plano: Conquer Valencia [16] by sending all troops from Murcia [15]. Reinforce Badajoz [4] from Santarem [1] and Faro [5], Madrid [12] from Salamanca [7], Vigo [10] from Porto [6], and Cordoba [11] from Sevilha [9]. Build knights in Lisboa, Santarem, Coimbra, Badajoz, Faro, Porto, Cordoba, Madrid, and archers in Evora, Salamanca, Sevilha, Vigo. Next turn, attack Toledo [8] from Badajoz and Burgos [14] from Vigo/Madrid.

A.depoimento: Our armies have struck at Castellon and Toledo, securing two key victories. While the enemy is distracted, we are quietly reinforcing our borders and building up our forces for the final push to 18 villages.
A.plano: Attack Castellon [18] from Valencia [16] and Toledo [8] from Badajoz [4]. Reinforce Madrid [12] from Salamanca [7], Vigo [10] from Porto [6], and Murcia [15] from Cordoba [11]. Build troops in all villages to prepare for the next wave of attacks on Burgos, Zaragoza, and Teruel.

B.depoimento: This turn, our armies strike across the map in a coordinated wave. Knights crush the enemy's archers, archers crush their spearmen. We take four enemy villages and strengthen our own defenses. The path to 18 villages is within reach, and our momentum is unstoppable.
B.plano: We are launching a coordinated offensive on all fronts. Our main attacks target Valencia, Madrid, Cordoba, and Vigo, using counter-tactics to maximize effectiveness. We reinforce Castellon and Tarragona to secure our borders, and shore up Zaragoza and Burgos after the attacks. After these victories, we will consolidate our gains and push towards the enemy capital, aiming to reach 18 villages as quickly as possible.

A.depoimento: King A launches a coordinated strike on Madrid and Cordoba to secure the border and push towards the enemy heartland. Reinforcements are sent to Vigo to prepare for the assault on Burgos, while the home villages work tirelessly to forge a mighty army for the next turn. The enemy will find no mercy as we march to victory!
A.plano: Attack Madrid [12] from Salamanca [7] and Cordoba [11] from Toledo [8], Sevilha [9], and Murcia [15]. Reinforce Vigo [10] from Porto [6] and move Lisbon's knights to Santarem [1]. Build maximum troops in all villages for next turn's push towards Zaragoza and Burgos. Do not attack Teruel [13] yet as its defense is too high.

A.depoimento: We have successfully consolidated our hold on Madrid and Cordoba. Now, we strike at Burgos [14] from Vigo [10] with our full might, exploiting the archer counter to their spearmen. At the same time, we are building up our forces across all villages and sending reinforcements to our border strongholds of Madrid and Toledo to prepare for the next phase of our campaign towards Zaragoza and Teruel.
A.plano: Conquer Burgos [14] from Vigo [10] this turn. Build maximum troops in all villages, especially Murcia [15] to prepare for the attack on Valencia [16] next turn. Send reinforcements from Salamanca [7] to Madrid [12] and from Cordoba [11] to Toledo [8] to build up forces for Zaragoza [17] and Teruel [13].

B.depoimento: This turn, I launch a triple offensive: Valencia sweeps Murcia, Teruel takes Toledo, and Zaragoza and Burgos converge on Madrid. I am pulling troops from the quiet eastern front to reinforce the western thrust, while my villages work overtime to produce knights for the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Conquer Madrid, Toledo, and Murcia this turn to secure the western frontier and cut enemy connections. Gather remaining forces from the east (Tarragona, Barcelona, Girona, Huesca) into Zaragoza and Burgos to prepare for the push into Vigo and the southern territories next turns. Build knights in all major villages to maintain offensive momentum.

A.depoimento: I have ordered a triple attack to expand my empire. My armies are marching on Toledo, Pamplona, and Valencia, while reinforcements strengthen my borders. I have also built new troops across my realm to ensure my dominance.
A.plano: Conquer Toledo, Pamplona, and Valencia this turn to expand my territory. Build 1 spearman and 1 archer in Murcia for the Valencia attack, and 2 archers in Burgos for defense. Reinforce Badajoz from Santarem, Salamanca from Coimbra, and Burgos from Vigo. Build 1 knight in all other villages to grow the army. Next turn, consolidate the new territories and prepare to attack Teruel or Zaragoza.

B.depoimento: This turn, I launch a three-pronged attack. From Madrid, I send forces to conquer the weakly defended Salamanca and the more heavily defended Burgos, leaving a strong garrison in Madrid. From Valencia, I commit all troops to take Murcia, while reinforcements from Teruel and Castellon secure Valencia against counterattack. I also send Pamplona's knight to Burgos. My villages produce a steady stream of knights and archers to fuel the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Conquer Salamanca, Burgos, and Murcia this turn to expand my territory. Send reinforcements to Valencia from Teruel and Castellon to secure the eastern front. Build knights and archers in all major villages to maintain offensive momentum. Next turn, push into Badajoz, Vigo, and the unexplored villages of Porto and Coimbra.

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered a coordinated strike across three fronts: Burgos to Vigo, Zaragoza to Pamplona, and Madrid to Salamanca. I sent my entire available force in these border villages to ensure overwhelming victory. To support the eastern flank, I redirected troops from Murcia and Teruel to Valencia, consolidating my defenses there. I also initiated a large-scale build program across my empire, producing knights, archers, and spearmen to replenish the ranks and prepare for the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: This turn, I will launch a massive multi-front offensive. Burgos will take Vigo, Zaragoza will take Pamplona, and Madrid will take Salamanca. Simultaneously, I will reinforce Valencia by sending troops from Murcia and Teruel to secure the eastern flank. After these victories, I will have 14 villages. Next, I will focus on building up troops in the newly conquered and emptied border villages (Burgos, Madrid, Zaragoza) to prepare for the assault on Toledo and Cordoba, which require heavier reinforcements. My ultimate goal is to push west towards the unexplored territories of Porto, Coimbra, and

A.depoimento: Statement: I have ordered a comprehensive military build-up, training archers and knights in every capable village to secure our borders and fuel our expansion. In a brilliant simultaneous offensive, my forces in Cordoba, Toledo, and Badajoz will strike Murcia, Teruel, Madrid, and Salamanca at the same time. In the north, I am reinforcing Pamplona with archers to hold the line, aiming to swell our ranks to 15 villages and bring us ever closer to victory.
A.plano: Plan: Build archers and knights across all villages to maximize growth. Launch a four-pronged offensive this turn: Cordoba takes Murcia, Toledo splits forces to take both Teruel and Madrid, and Badajoz's full knight army conquers Salamanca. Reinforce Pamplona with 4 archers and hold all troops there to defend against the incoming enemy army. Next turn, we will have 15 villages and can target Burgos, Zaragoza, and Vigo to reach the 18-victory threshold.

A.depoimento: Statement: This turn, we are launching a precise strike on Zaragoza to expand our territory, while strategically sending reinforcements from Toledo to Madrid and from Salamanca to Porto. This will strengthen our borders and prepare our armies for the next wave of conquests, bringing us closer to the 18-victory threshold.
A.plano: Plan: We are focusing on reinforcing our border villages Madrid and Porto while taking Zaragoza with Madrid's current troops. Next turn, we will use the reinforced Madrid to take Burgos, and the reinforced Porto to take Vigo. We will also prepare to take Castellon from Teruel.

B.depoimento: I have ordered a multi-pronged assault on the enemy's vulnerable positions. Valencia's knights and archers are striking at Teruel, while Vigo's full army marches on Porto to open the western front. At the same time, Tarragona and Pamplona are sending their best troops to reinforce Zaragoza and Burgos, setting the stage for the inevitable attack on Madrid next turn. Every village is working at full capacity to feed the war machine.
B.plano: Launch a coordinated strike on the enemy's weak central front. This turn, Valencia's army attacks Teruel while Vigo's forces assault Porto. Simultaneously, Tarragona and Pamplona send reinforcements to Zaragoza and Burgos to prepare for the attack on Madrid next turn. All villages are building troops to maintain the offensive momentum. After taking Madrid and Teruel, push towards Toledo and Cordoba to reach the 18-village threshold for victory.

B.depoimento: We launch a decisive double strike this turn! Teruel's forces crush the weak garrison in Toledo, while Zaragoza and Burgos coordinate a massive assault on Madrid, the enemy's central hub. Reinforcements pour into Zaragoza and Teruel to secure our gains. With Madrid and Toledo in our grasp, we are on the verge of splitting the enemy's territory and marching toward victory!
B.plano: This turn, we launch a coordinated double offensive on the enemy's weak central front. Teruel's garrison assaults Toledo, while Zaragoza and Burgos coordinate a massive strike on Madrid. Valencia, Tarragona, and Huesca reinforce Teruel and Zaragoza to secure the captured territories. Vigo and Pamplona bolster Burgos's defense. Once Madrid and Toledo fall, we will have 13 villages and a solid foothold in the enemy heartland. Next, we will push south to Cordoba and west to Badajoz, aiming to reach the 18-village threshold for victory.

A.depoimento: I have launched a double attack on Vigo and Valencia, sending the bulk of my forces from Porto and Murcia. At the same time, I am reinforcing Badajoz and Salamanca to prepare for next turn's assaults on Toledo and Madrid. My villages are busy building troops to replenish my ranks and ensure I have the manpower to hold my new conquests.
A.plano: Attack Vigo from Porto and Valencia from Murcia this turn. Reinforce Badajoz from Santarem and Salamanca from Coimbra to launch attacks on Toledo and Madrid next turn. Build troops in all villages to grow the army.

B.depoimento: Orders are given: Toledo strikes at Cordoba, Madrid assaults Salamanca. Reinforcements pour into Valencia from Castellon, Teruel, Zaragoza, and the eastern interior, while Burgos bolsters Vigo. We are closing the net on the enemy's western and southern fronts.
B.plano: This turn, we launch coordinated attacks on Cordoba from Toledo and Salamanca from Madrid. We reinforce Valencia with troops from Castellon, Teruel, Zaragoza, and the eastern interior to prepare for the assault on Murcia. We also send reinforcements from Burgos to Vigo to prepare for the attack on Porto. Our goal is to capture Cordoba and Salamanca this turn, bringing our total to 15 villages, and then push towards Murcia and Porto to reach the 18-village threshold for victory.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launch a multi-pronged offensive against the enemy's weak borders. Badajoz strikes Toledo, Sevilha targets Cordoba, and Vigo attacks Burgos. Porto sends reinforcements to aid Coimbra's ongoing assault on Salamanca. We rebuild our forces with a focus on archers to replenish our losses.
A.plano: Focus on expanding south and east. Attack Toledo from Badajoz, Cordoba from Sevilha, and Burgos from Vigo. Reinforce Salamanca from Porto. Build archers in all major villages to rebuild the army.

B.depoimento: This turn, we attacked Murcia from Valencia and Porto from Salamanca, taking both enemy villages. We reinforced our borders with troops from interior villages, built new troops, and prepared for the enemy's expected attack on Salamanca. We are on track to reach 18 villages.
B.plano: We are launching attacks on Murcia and Porto to increase our village count to 16. We are reinforcing Salamanca, Cordoba, and Burgos to defend against enemy counterattacks and to prepare for future attacks on Coimbra and Vigo. We are building troops in all villages and sending reinforcements to the border. Our next goal is to take Coimbra and Vigo to reach 18 villages and secure victory.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launched attacks on Vigo and Coimbra, capturing both villages and increasing our count to 15. We reinforced Madrid, Teruel, and Burgos with troops from Zaragoza, Valencia, and Pamplona. We built knights and archers across our empire to prepare for the next phase of the campaign. Our focus is now on consolidating our borders and gathering a massive army in Valencia for the next offensive.
B.plano: We are attacking Vigo from Burgos and Coimbra from Porto to capture two villages and reach 15. We are reinforcing Madrid, Teruel, and Burgos to defend against enemy counterattacks. We are building knights and archers in all villages to grow our army. Next, we will gather forces in Valencia and launch an attack on Cordoba or Toledo to capture more villages and move towards the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: I launched a coordinated attack on Coimbra and Madrid, utilizing counter tactics to overcome their defenses. Simultaneously, I reinforced my border villages to protect against enemy counterattacks and built up my reserves for future campaigns.
A.plano: Capture Coimbra and Madrid using counter tactics (archers vs spearmen, knights vs archers). Reinforce Salamanca, Toledo, Cordoba, and Badajoz to secure borders against enemy counterattacks. Build archers and knights to grow the army for next turn's expansion.

B.depoimento: I am building up my forces for a major push on the western front. Coimbra is producing spearmen for the attack on Salamanca next turn. Valencia's knights are marching to Murcia to prepare for a decisive assault on Cordoba. Reinforcements are flowing from Vigo to Porto and from Burgos to Madrid to secure my borders. The plan is clear: take Salamanca next turn, then Cordoba, and push towards 18 villages.
B.plano: Focus on the western front. Build 4 spearmen in Coimbra to attack Salamanca (defense 15) next turn with 5 spearmen, 1 archer, 1 knight — spearman counters knight for x1.5 bonus, giving attack 16.5 > 15. Send 8 knights from Valencia to Murcia to prepare for Cordoba attack (defense 25) with knight counter for overwhelming force. Reinforce Porto from Vigo and Madrid from Burgos to secure borders. After Salamanca, push to Santarem from Coimbra. Target: reach 18 villages within 3-4 turns.

A.depoimento: Our forces strike at Coimbra and Madrid simultaneously. The Santarem army overruns Coimbra's defenses, while the Toledo and Salamanca armies converge on Madrid to eliminate its garrison. Reinforcements are dispatched to secure the borders against counterattacks.
A.plano: Capture Coimbra with Santarem's troops. Send reinforcements from Lisboa to Santarem to hold the border. Launch a two-wave assault on Madrid: the existing march from Toledo will weaken the garrison, followed by a strong force from Toledo and a supporting force from Salamanca. Reinforce Salamanca from Badajoz. Build knights and archers to replenish losses and prepare for the next expansion.

A.depoimento: I ordered the assault on Zaragoza from Madrid, sending 4 archers and 2 knights while leaving 5 archers and 1 knight to hold the city. I reinforced my borders: Coimbra received troops from Lisboa and Santarem, Madrid from Salamanca, Toledo from Badajoz, and Cordoba from Sevilha. I built 2 knights in Madrid and Coimbra, and archers across my villages to grow my army. My goal is to expand into Zaragoza and then target Teruel and Burgos.
A.plano: Capture Zaragoza with Madrid's troops, leaving a garrison. Reinforce Coimbra from Lisboa and Santarem to defend against Porto. Reinforce Madrid from Salamanca, Toledo from Badajoz, and Cordoba from Sevilha. Build knights in Madrid and Coimbra, and archers across villages. Next turn, attack Teruel or Burgos with reinforced armies.

B.depoimento: King B strikes on two fronts this turn! From Teruel, our spearman and archers march on Toledo, whose garrison of knights is no match for our counter-tipped spearhead. Simultaneously, from Porto, our forces assault Coimbra, crushing its archer defense. We are building knights and archers in every single village to ensure our army grows faster than the enemy's. The road to Lisbon is opening up!
B.plano: We are focusing on the southern and central fronts. This turn, we launch a double offensive: Teruel attacks the weakly defended Toledo (defense 5), while Porto sweeps into Coimbra (defense 13). These two victories will bring us to 15 villages. In parallel, we are building a knight/archer core in every village to swell our ranks. We are reinforcing Zaragoza and Burgos from the interior to prepare for the push on Madrid, and moving troops from Valencia and Castellon to Teruel to sustain the momentum towards Cordoba and the capital. Our goal is to secure 18 villages by turn 30.

A.depoimento: Our armies strike at Porto and Toledo, overwhelming their garrisons. Simultaneously, we march reinforcements to Madrid and Coimbra to secure our borders. The enemy is caught between our hammer and anvil.
A.plano: Capture Porto and Toledo this turn to expand our territory and increase production. Reinforce Madrid from Salamanca and Coimbra from Lisboa to prepare for future attacks. Build troops in all villages to grow our army. Next turn, attack Zaragoza from Madrid and possibly Burgos from Toledo.

A.depoimento: I've ordered a full build across all twelve villages — knights everywhere I can afford, plus extra archers in Porto and Toledo. Two armies are on the march: Porto's force strikes at Vigo, whose pitiful defense of 5 can't stop us, while Madrid's archers and knights descend on Zaragoza. If both fall, we'll hold 14 villages and be well positioned to push deeper into enemy territory toward Burgos and Teruel.
A.plano: Build knights in every village to grow the army; Porto makes 1 knight + 2 archers, Toledo makes 3 archers due to iron limits. Attack Vigo from Porto (defense 5, very weak) and Zaragoza from Madrid (defense 18) to gain 2 villages and reach 14 of 24. Keep small garrisons at Porto and Madrid for defense. Next turn: assess losses, push toward Burgos and Teruel, and send reinforcements from Coimbra/Salamanca to the border.
